scores.rationale: The stylized fact links intraspecific scaling of maximum oxygen use to morphology/transport network design. Several snippets bear on this. Snippet 13 explicitly contrasts MTE's transport-network assumptions (detailed distribution network design predicting oxygen delivery scaling) with DEB. Snippet 17 derives that dioxygen consumption scales as V^alpha with alpha in [2/3,1] as a linear combination of surface-area (2/3) and volume (1) terms, directly tying the exponent to geometric/morphological considerations. Snippet 5 shows ontogenetic (intraspecific) scaling differs from interspecific scaling and is explained by shape/morphology arguments. Snippet 18 demonstrates that respiration can deviate from 3/4 (e.g., proportional to sqrt of biomass in encrusting bryozoans), consistent with morphology-dependent scaling. Snippet 16 explicitly qualifies the 3/4 power as holding 'by isomorphs,' implying shape dependence. The remaining snippets restate the 3/4 rule or describe oxygen as derived from mass balance without bearing on network morphology, hence neutral. No snippet contradicts the fact. Overall there is moderate, consistent support with no conflict, but the evidence is somewhat indirect and scattered rather than a single decisive demonstration.
